name: Jimson Weed
description: Jimson Weed (Datura stramonium), also called thorn apple or devil’s trumpet, is extremely toxic to cats. Every part of the plant can be dangerous, including the leaves, seeds, flowers, and stems. The plant contains tropane alkaloids such as atropine, scopolamine, and hyoscyamine. These chemicals block normal nerve signals in the body. Even a small exposure can affect the heart, brain, eyes, gut, and body temperature. Signs can include wide pupils, drooling or dry mouth, vomiting, fast heartbeat, agitation, weakness, tremors, seizures, or collapse. This is an emergency. If your cat chews or eats any part of Jimson weed, contact a veterinarian or emergency clinic immediately.
safetyNotes: Toxic compounds: tropane alkaloids — atropine, scopolamine, hyoscyamine; all parts toxic; spiky seed pods most concentrated
Mechanism: competitive antagonism of muscarinic acetylcholine receptors, causing full anticholinergic syndrome (dry, fast, hot, blind, mad)
Symptoms: dilated pupils (mydriasis), dry mouth, rapid heart rate (tachycardia), elevated body temperature, disorientation, agitation, hallucination-like behaviour, seizures, coma
The seed pods are the most concentrated source and can persist on the ground for months
Any suspected ingestion is a veterinary emergency — tropane alkaloid poisoning can be rapidly fatal
